label: verify-q1-mechanisms

claims.claim: Reporter-assay studies disagree. Martinez-Ara (mouse) finds most CREs promoter-selective.
claims.source_says: More than half of the tested CREs exhibit significant promoter selectivity.
claims.note: Abstract matches; the Tan 2026 preprint also says recent reporter studies reached contradictory conclusions.

claims.claim: Bergman (human) finds most enhancers activate all promoters similarly, multiplicative (R2 0.82). Tan 2026 preprint reports a similar rank order with promoter-specific power-law exponents.
claims.source_says: most enhancers activate all promoters by similar amounts, and intrinsic enhancer and promoter activities multiplicatively combine to determine RNA output (R2 = 0.82). Tan: enhancers activate all promoters in a similar rank order; exponent varying across promoters.
claims.note: Both the Nature abstract and the bioRxiv abstract (10.64898/2026.06.25.734173) match.

claims.claim: Martinez-Ara say their basal-activity trend cannot separate saturation from lower enhancer dependence, so published data leave saturation vs compatibility open.
claims.source_says: This suggests a saturation effect, or it could indicate that promoters with high basal activity are less dependent on distal enhancers.
claims.note: The quote is verbatim, but it is about boost indices vs basal activity; the 'published data leave saturation vs compatibility open' conclusion is the agent's inference.

claims.claim: Saturation (monotone promoter response) can tie enhancer order but not reverse it; reversal needs a second latent. Proved in core Lean; Spearman disattenuated 0.56 Klf2, 0.83 Nanog, 0.62 Tfcp2l1.
claims.source_says: Lean: no_reversal (monotone g p, g p (s e') < g p (s e) implies not g q (s e) < g q (s e')); two_latent_reverses. ma_results.json medians: Klf2 0.555, Nanog 0.832, Tfcp2l1 0.617.
claims.note: Theorem statements match the plain words and the JSON values round to the claimed numbers; Lean and the analysis were not re-run.

overall: All four key claims hold. Claim 3 is partly supported because its closing inference goes beyond the quoted sentence. The two papers and the Tan preprint abstract were checked via Europe PMC and the bioRxiv API, and the Martinez-Ara full text was checked for the saturation passage.
